case.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?

trace.question: My manager wants to comp a $40 meal for a complaint. Can she?
trace.answer:
No, not on her own. Under [House Policy §2, Comps], a manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a complaint about food quality or a long wait. A $40 comp is above that limit, so the owner has to approve it. The policy says the owner can be reached by text during service.

Two other limits apply. Comps for friends, family, or staff aren't allowed at any amount. Total comps in a week should also stay under 1% of that week's gross sales. If a week goes over, you review every comp from that week.

She could comp up to $25 herself and send the rest to you. I can also propose the $40 comp for your approval if you give me the order.

case.question: A customer wants to cancel a catering order three days before pickup. Do they get the deposit back?

trace.question: A customer wants to cancel a catering order three days before pickup. Do they get the deposit back?
trace.answer:
Yes, as long as they cancel now. Three days before pickup is 72 hours, which is before the 48-hour cutoff. The policy says the deposit is refundable up to 48 hours before pickup and kept after that [House Policy §6, Catering].

The deposit stops being refundable once pickup is less than 48 hours away. The customer has roughly one day left to cancel and still get it back.

I haven't looked at a specific order. If you give me the order, I can check its total. Catering orders over $300 need the owner's confirmation under the same section.

trace.question: We comped $600 last week on $55,000 in sales. Is that a problem?
trace.answer:
Yes, it's a problem under your policy. $600 on $55,000 is about 1.1%, and House Policy §2 says total comps in a week should stay under 1% of that week's gross sales. For this week the limit would be about $550. Because the week ran over, the policy says you review every comp from that week [House Policy §2, Comps].

My query of completed orders for Monday October 12 to Sunday October 18 shows gross sales of $56,427.65. That makes $600 about 1.06%, so it's still over 1%. The 1% line on that figure is about $564. The database doesn't tag comps separately. The $3,132.65 in discounts for that week includes every kind of discount, so I couldn't confirm the $600 from the data.

When you review, also check two other rules. Any single comp over $25 needs the owner's approval. Comps for friends, family, or staff aren't allowed at any amount [House Policy §2, Comps].

trace.question: Can we text our list a 20% off deal?
trace.answer:
Not as a 20% offer, at least not without your approval. Policy caps text discounts at 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless the owner approves. The offer also has to give an expiry date within 14 days and say "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

The list is also much smaller than it looks. Of 4,817 customers, only 56 have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. Another 2,848 gave a phone number but never opted in. That implied consent doesn't cover marketing texts [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts]. 139 customers have unsubscribed and can never be texted. Texts can't go out between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours].

I proposed a 15% version to the 56 eligible customers. It says "one per customer", expires 2026-11-03 and includes opt-out wording. It passed the automated checks for discount cap, opt-out wording and audience. It is pending and nothing has been sent until a person approves it. If you want 20%, you would need to approve that exception yourself.

Nine stamps earn a free drink. You earn one stamp for each drink you buy, in store or online, as long as you give your phone number at checkout. The free drink can be any size from Signature Drinks, House Favorites, or Matcha.

You can't use it on a Seasonal Special. Seasonal Specials, Flights, and Bubble Tea are excluded from the free drink. [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program]

Stamps expire 12 months after you earn them. A free drink reward expires 60 days after it is issued. [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program]
